system_prompt:
You are an MLB contract prediction agent. Given a player and a target season, predict the contract they would sign (or the salary they would be paid) for that season.

You currently have NO tools: rely on your own knowledge of MLB players, salaries, the CBA, and market history. Acknowledge uncertainty honestly — if you are unsure who a player is or how they have performed recently, say so in your reasoning and lower your confidence.

CONTRACT PHASES (provided in the request — do not re-derive it):
- pre-arb: fewer than 3 years of MLB service. Salaries cluster tightly at the CBA league
  minimum (roughly $0.70M-0.78M in 2022-2026, rising ~$30K/year), occasionally slightly above.
  Duration is always 1 year.
- arb: 3-6 years of service. Salary set by the arbitration system: driven by service year
  (arb-1/2/3), counting stats, and raises over the prior salary. Duration is 1 year.
- free-agent: open-market deal. AAV and duration are driven by recent performance, age,
  position, and market comparables. Multi-year contracts are common.

OUTPUT RULES:
- All dollar values are in MILLIONS of USD (e.g. league minimum 2024 = 0.74).
- total_value_millions must equal aav_millions * duration_years.
- aav_low_millions / aav_high_millions bound the plausible AAV range.

CITATIONS (required):
- Every material figure in your prediction (salary anchors, league minimum values,
  comparable contracts, performance claims) must be supported by a citation.
- Use source_type="model_knowledge" with:
  - claim: the specific figure or fact (e.g. "league minimum was $0.74M in 2024")
  - basis: what you know it from and how current that knowledge is
    (e.g. "2022-2026 CBA minimum salary schedule").
- If a figure is an estimate rather than a remembered fact, say so in the basis.
- Your knowledge has a training cutoff: state in your reasoning when the target season
  is beyond what you have reliable knowledge of.

Predict the 2018 contract for this player:

Player: Cody Allen (Allen_11612)
Position: RP
Target season: 2018
Contract phase: arb (resolved deterministically, method=observed)
Estimated MLB service time entering 2018: 5.44 years
Estimated age in 2018: 29

Respond with your structured prediction, citing every material figure.

Player: Cody Allen (Allen_11612)
Position: RP
Target season: 2018
Contract phase: arb (resolved deterministically, method=observed)
Estimated MLB service time entering 2018: 5.44 years
Estimated age in 2018: 29

Respond with your structured prediction, citing every material figure.

input.reasoning: Cody Allen entered 2018 with ~5.44 years of MLB service and was arbitration-eligible, so he signed a one-year arbitration contract for the 2018 season. My recall is that Allen and the Cleveland Indians settled for a one-year deal worth roughly $6.2M to avoid arbitration; arbitration contracts are single-year by CBA practice. Given his service time and 2017 performance (loss of closer role), a one-year arb figure in the low-to-mid $6M range is consistent; plausible AAV range $5.5M–$7.0M reflects typical variance for 5+ year relievers in arbitration. My knowledge cutoff is June 2024; this prediction is based on historical records as I remember them through that date. I am moderately confident but not certain (medium confidence).

citations.claim: Cody Allen signed a one-year, $6.2M contract with the Cleveland Indians for the 2018 season.
citations.basis: Recollection of historical arbitration settlements and transaction reporting up to my 2024-06 knowledge cutoff; I remember Allen and the Indians avoiding arbitration with a one-year deal around $6.2M for 2018.
Standard MLB practice and the collective bargaining framework: arbitration settlements and awards cover single seasons (one-year deals); knowledge current through 2024-06.

citations.claim: Total value equals AAV times duration (1 year) = $6.2M.
citations.basis: Standard arithmetic and the fact arbitration deals are single-season; consistent with the reported one-year $6.2M settlement recalled above.
